question: A shopkeeper marked a watch at ₹800. He sold it after allowing a 15% discount. If his profit on the sale was 20%, what was the cost price of the watch?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the direct ratio relation between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP):

⇒ CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP / 800 = (100 − 15) / (100 + 20) = 85 / 120

⇒ CP = 800 × (85 / 120) = 1700 / 3

⇒ CP ≈ 566.67

**∴ The correct answer is ₹566.67.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹800

Discount = 15%

Profit = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount% of MP)

Cost Price (CP) = (SP × 100) / (100 + Profit%)

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 
 
 SP = ₹680
 
 
 MP = ₹800

 
• 
 +20% Profit
 
 
• 
 −15% Discount

 CP = ₹680 × (100 / 120) = ₹566.67

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 800 − (15 / 100) × 800

⇒ SP = 800 − 120 = ₹680

⇒ CP = (SP × 100) / (100 + 20)

⇒ CP = (680 × 100) / 120

⇒ CP = 68000 / 120

⇒ CP = 1700 / 3 ≈ ₹566.67

**∴ The correct answer is ₹566.67.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct CP and MP Ratio

A very useful formula linking Cost Price and Marked Price directly without calculating the Selling Price intermediate is: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are offered, the equivalent single discount is given by the successive percentage formula: (x + y − xy / 100)%.

MarkUp Percentage

MarkUp is the initial amount added to the Cost Price to set the Marked Price. It is always calculated on the base of Cost Price: MarkUp% = ((MP − CP) / CP) × 100.
